SAMPLE HIRING AND EMPLOYEE REFERRAL PROCESS - INDIA
1. The hiring manager defines the role, required skills, location, and approved salary range.
2. HR confirms budget and approvals before publishing the vacancy.
3. Apply through the careers page using the instructions in the job posting.
4. For an employee referral, ask the employee to submit your resume through the internal referral portal.
5. Include your name, contact details, job title or requisition ID, and an up-to-date resume.
6. The referring employee should get your consent before sharing your contact details or resume.
7. Do not send confidential information from a current or former employer.
8. HR reviews applications against the role requirements and contacts shortlisted candidates.
9. Interviews may include a recruiter screen, role-related interviews, and a practical assessment.
10. Interviewers submit job-related feedback using consistent evaluation criteria.
11. HR verifies references or other details only where applicable and with required consent.
12. The selected candidate receives a written offer after internal approvals are complete.
13. Referral rewards, if offered, depend on the current referral policy and eligibility conditions.
14. The referrer should not promise an interview, offer, or referral reward.
15. Hiring decisions are based on role fit and must comply with company policy and applicable law.

SAMPLE RESIGNATION AND OFFBOARDING PROCESS - INDIA
1. Check your appointment letter and HR policy for the notice period that applies to your role.
2. A sample company default is 30 calendar days for most roles; some roles may require 60 or 90 days.
3. Your signed employment terms and applicable law take precedence over this example.
4. Send a dated resignation email to your manager and HR, stating your proposed last working day.
5. Ask HR to acknowledge the resignation and confirm the notice end date in writing.
6. Do not assume notice can be shortened or waived; obtain written approval from HR.
7. Any notice buyout or adjustment of leave against notice must be approved and follow policy and law.
8. Agree on a handover plan with your manager, including owners, deadlines, and current project status.
9. Return company laptop, access card, keys, and other property by the agreed date.
10. Transfer work files only through approved company systems; do not copy confidential data personally.
11. Submit outstanding expense claims and complete timesheets or leave requests before your final day.
12. HR will explain final salary, eligible leave settlement, benefits, and required exit documents.
13. Complete the exit checklist and attend an exit discussion if requested.
14. Ask HR for a service or experience letter and any tax or payroll documents you need.
15. Keep personal contact and bank details current for final payroll and post-employment communication.

SAMPLE EMPLOYEE REIMBURSEMENT PROCESS - INDIA
1. Check the current travel and expense policy before spending; limits vary by role and location.
2. Get written manager approval in advance for travel, equipment, training, or unusual expenses.
3. Use the company booking method for flights and hotels when one is provided.
4. Pay only for reasonable, necessary business expenses; personal costs are not reimbursable.
5. Keep itemized bills or tax invoices showing the supplier, date, items, and amount.
6. For travel, retain approved itineraries and receipts for transport, lodging, and other eligible costs.
7. For card or UPI payments, include the itemized bill as well as proof of payment when requested.
8. Submit the claim in the company's expense portal within 30 days of the expense or trip ending.
9. Select the correct expense category and enter the business purpose, date, amount, and cost centre.
10. Attach readable receipts and the approval record; explain any missing receipt in the claim.
11. Submit expenses in INR; disclose the original currency and exchange-rate evidence for foreign costs.
12. The manager checks business purpose and approval; Finance checks receipts and policy compliance.
13. Respond promptly if Finance returns the claim for missing information or clarification.
14. Approved claims are paid to the registered payroll or bank account, typically in the next expense cycle.
15. Never split, duplicate, or misrepresent a claim; contact Finance about exceptions before submitting.

SAMPLE LEAVE POLICY - INDIA
1. This is an illustrative company policy; applicable state law and the employee handbook take precedence.
2. Example annual allowance for a full-time employee: 15 earned/privilege leave days.
3. Example annual allowance: 12 casual leave days and 12 sick leave days.
4. Allowances may be prorated for employees joining or leaving during the year.
5. Earned leave accrues monthly; HR should confirm balances and carry-forward limits.
6. Casual leave is intended for short personal needs and is normally not carried forward.
7. Notify your manager promptly when taking sick leave; provide a medical certificate if policy requires it.
8. Apply for planned leave in the HR portal, selecting dates and the leave category.
9. Request planned leave at least five working days in advance where possible.
10. Wait for manager approval before treating planned leave as confirmed.
11. For an emergency, contact your manager as soon as possible and submit the HR portal request afterward.
12. Coordinate work handover before taking an extended leave.
13. Public holidays follow the location-specific company calendar and are separate from these example balances.
14. Maternity, paternity, adoption, and other statutory leave follow applicable law and company policy.
15. Leave encashment, carry-forward, and balances are governed by applicable law and the official policy.
